$comment: Every screenshot the site and the README use for the LOADER, keyed by id. Hand-written, and content rather than provenance: no stage, no scene, no timestamp, no game version. Files of record live in screenshots/ as PNG, which is what the README links so GitHub can render them. They sit at the repository root rather than under docs/ because they are neither documentation nor site-only: the README and the site both consume them, and a docs/ holding nothing but images collided with site/content/docs/, which holds the actual authoring pages. An ADDON's screenshot is not here and must not be: it is declared by that addon's own addon.json and lives in its directory, so the manager can show it too and the alt text has one home. The site generates its own AVIF and WebP derivatives at build time and never commits them. `minWidth` is what the shot needs to supply. For a full window it is the widest display box it appears in, times two for a retina display. For a fixed-size HUD panel captured at 2x it is the capture itself, because such a panel CANNOT be captured wider without zooming the game, and holding it to a column width would report a permanent shortfall nobody can act on; the build warns when a file is narrower and caps the figure at natural size so it renders smaller and sharp rather than upscaled and soft. Alt text is written once, here, and never in a template.

game-menu.caption: Game Menu · Addons, added by the loader
game-menu.alt: The in-game Game Menu listing Key Bindings, Controller, Graphics, Interface, Audio, Performance Overlay, Report a Bug, Unstuck, Logout and Return to Game, with a new Addons entry at the bottom, above the game's version readout.

install-confirm.caption: The install prompt, in the game
install-confirm.alt: The Browse tab showing an install confirmation for Cooldown Bars. It lists what the addon says it needs to do, then a gold warning that the declared list is what the author says the addon is for, not a limit the loader enforces, and that addon code runs with the same access to the page as the game itself, including your login token.

chrome-user-scripts.alt: The Allow User Scripts row on a Chrome extension's details page, switched on, with Chrome's own warning that the extension will be able to run code which has not been reviewed by Google.
